title: ING-VP: MLLMs cannot Play Easy Vision-based Games Yet

paper.authors: Haoran Zhang, Hangyu Guo, Shuyue Guo, Meng Cao, Wenhao Huang, Jiaheng Liu, Ge Zhang
paper.repo_license: none - no LICENSE file at the repository root (GitHub reports no licence), so the code is all-rights-reserved by default
paper.other_artifacts: The repository carries the full benchmark inline: data/<game>/levels_50.{txt,jsonl} (50 levels each for maze, sokoban, n_queens, n_puzzle, hanoi, sudoku = 300 levels), data/<game>/LevelImages/level_*.png, the game engines under game/, reference solvers under src/solver/, and all 36 prompts under prompts/. outputs/ is gitignored, so no model outputs are released. Upstream level sources: Sokoban from David W. Skinner's Sasquatch sets, Sudoku from a Kaggle '4 million sudoku puzzles' dataset.

dependence.note: The models are the object of study and every number is a deterministic function of their outputs plus a rule-based game engine - no human raters and no LLM judge. GPT-4 Turbo is one of seven closed-source arms; it is the only GPT-4-class arm in the table with a still-callable snapshot, and uniquely among the closed models it was evaluated in the text-only settings only (all three image-text cells are 'null'), which puts it inside our text-only runner.

claim.statement: GPT-4 Turbo solves almost none of ING-VP's 300 easy game levels in the text-only settings: 2.30% accuracy in multi-step without history, 2.30% with history and 1.00% in one-step, averaging 1.87% (Table 1; per-game breakdown in Table 3, where every point comes from maze at 14.00% in the two multi-step settings and from sokoban/n_queens/n_puzzle at 2.00% each in one-step, with hanoi and sudoku at 0.00% throughout) - below the benchmark's best model, Claude-3.5 Sonnet at 3.37%, and consistent with the paper's thesis that current MLLMs lack spatial imagination and multi-step planning.
claim.metric: Accuracy = share of the 50 levels per game solved within the step budget (MAX_STEPS = 50 for multi-step; a single action sequence for one-step), averaged over the six games; the game engine under game/<name>/ decides completion. Secondary metrics in the same rows: completion degree (Comp.) and action efficiency (Eff.), both produced by src/multi_step/score.py, src/one_step/score.py and src/summary.py.
claim.original_source: Paper Table 1 (Main results, row 'GPT-4 Turbo'), Table 3 in Appendix C ('Results for all of the MLLMs', per-game breakdown). Column order taken from src/summary.py's tasks list.

protocol.model_usage_verified: partial - Table 2 lists 'GPT-4 Turbo' with only the generic platform.openai.com model-page link, and src/model.py asks a third-party gateway (OpenAI client with base_url redacted to 'xxxx') for the string 'gpt-4-turbo-128k', which is not an OpenAI model id. The date rule applies to the paper's undated 'GPT-4 Turbo' in an October 2024 preprint and resolves it to gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09; the '128k' string is a gateway alias and leaves residual doubt (128k context was the headline of the retired gpt-4-1106-preview).
protocol.endpoint: Original: an unnamed OpenAI-compatible proxy (src/model.py APIInferencer.load_client with api_key='xxxx', base_url='xxxx'). Re-run: POST https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions with the same message shape.
protocol.prompt_source: prompts/multi_step_text/prt_<game>_{system_prompt,instruction}.txt for the two multi-step settings (with prt_<game>_text_history.txt under prompts/multi_step_history_text/), prompts/one_step_text/prt_<game>_os_text.txt for one-step; all 36 prompts are also printed in Appendix B.

messages.content: multi-step only: prt_<game>_system_prompt.txt, e.g. maze 'You are a player of Maze game. And you will be given a text matrix ... Use JSON as your output format: {"output": "L"} ... Output only one move at a time, wait for confirmation before proceeding to the next step.'
multi-step: prt_<game>_instruction.txt with {text_representation_path} replaced by the board; one-step: prt_<game>_os_text.txt with the board, no system message (src/one_step/infer.py passes '')

params.temperature_source: run.sh passes --temperature 0 for all four multi-step modes; src/one_step/infer.py hard-codes 0 in inferencer.infer('', prompt, image_path, 0). The paper itself never states a decoding setting.

protocol.calls_per_item: one-step 1; multi-step up to 51 (while step <= MAX_STEPS and not solved), and with ~2% solve rates almost every level runs the full budget
protocol.evaluation: Fully automatic and offline: the per-game engines game/<name>/<name>_ms.py apply the parsed JSON action and report validity, then src/multi_step/score.py, src/one_step/score.py, the matching completion.py files and src/summary.py emit acc/comp/eff CSVs into outputs/*/final and outputs/summary. Actions are extracted from the reply with a regular expression looking for the JSON {"output": ...} form.
protocol.environment: Python with openai==1.51.2, Pillow, pygame (needed only for the image settings); no GPU for the GPT arm. Two small edits are required before anything can run: set a real api_key/base_url in src/model.py, and add 'gpt4turbo' to the --model-name argparse choices (the factory dict knows the key but argparse rejects it).

artifacts.data_path: data/<game>/levels_50.txt (maze, sokoban) and levels_50.jsonl (n_queens, n_puzzle, hanoi, sudoku), 50 levels each, in-repo; data/<game>/LevelImages/*.png for the image settings (not needed here)
artifacts.eval_path: src/multi_step/score.py, src/multi_step/completion.py, src/one_step/score.py, src/one_step/completion.py, src/summary.py; game engines under game/; reference solvers under src/solver/
artifacts.data_license: unstated - the repository has no LICENSE; the Sokoban levels come from David W. Skinner's published sets and the Sudoku levels from a Kaggle dataset, both with their own terms
artifacts.redistributable: no - treat as fetch-at-run-time; the levels ship inside an unlicensed repository and two games' levels are derived from third-party puzzle collections
artifacts.notes: outputs/ is gitignored, so no per-level GPT-4 Turbo transcripts or per-step states were released: drift can only be measured against the published acc/comp/eff numbers. The benchmark is self-contained otherwise - engines, solvers, prompts and levels are all present and the text settings need no images.

blockers: Cost: the full text-only protocol is ~30,300 calls per seed (300 levels x up to 50 steps x 2 multi-step settings, plus 300 one-step calls), about $236 per seed and ~$708 at 3 seeds. The card is only cheap if it is scoped down (see budget and user_checks).

Two live bugs in the released multi-step text path that shaped the published numbers and that a faithful re-run would reproduce. (1) Frozen board: process_level() reassigns `prompt = add_level_to_prompt(prompt, ...)` inside the step loop, so after step 1 the {text_representation_path} placeholder is gone and the .replace() is a no-op - the model is shown the initial board for all 50 steps while the engine advances the real state. (2) Empty history: add_conversation_history() reads outputs/multi_step/history/models/... but config.py writes text history to outputs/multi_step/text_only/history, so the file never exists and {conversation_history_path} is replaced by an empty string. Together these make the 'multi-step with history' and 'without history' text conditions the same prompt, which matches the identical published accuracies (2.30 / 2.30, per-game 14.00 0 0 0 0 0 in both) for GPT-4 Turbo and for Claude-3 Opus.

Model-identifier confusion in src/model.py: two classes are both named GPT4TurboInference, and the second definition - the one Python keeps, and the one the factory dict binds to the key 'gpt4turbo' - asks the gateway for 'claude3_opus'. Running the released code unmodified with --model-name gpt4turbo would therefore query Claude 3 Opus, which is also the row whose accuracies match GPT-4 Turbo's exactly (1.87 average in both). The class must be repaired before the GPT arm can be run at all.

Snapshot is a gateway alias: the code names 'gpt-4-turbo-128k' against a redacted base_url, not an OpenAI snapshot, so the mapping to gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 rests on the date rule rather than on the code.

APIInferencer.model_chat retries by unbounded recursion on any exception and get_correct_response recurses whenever the reply is falsy - with a dead or rate-limited endpoint this is an infinite loop and a budget hazard; it needs a bounded-retry wrapper before any paid run.

baseline_alive.purpose: live baseline (P0): the three text-only settings of the GPT-4 Turbo row

dead_comparators_not_runnable: gpt-4o-2024-05-13 and gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 are alive but were run only in the image-text settings plus text-only, i.e. they would need the multimodal path for a full row

budget.assumptions: Full text-only protocol at 3 seeds. Prompt sizes measured from the repository: multi-step system+instruction+board averages 1,194 characters (~340 tokens) across the six games, one-step 987 characters (~280 tokens). Multi-step without history: 15,000 calls/seed at ~360 in / ~15 out = $61/seed. Multi-step with history: the accumulated 'step N: {output}' log adds ~750 tokens on average by the end of a 50-step level, so ~1,110 in / ~15 out = $173/seed (this is the cost the empty-history bug does NOT actually incur - if the bug is reproduced faithfully the history arm costs the same $61 as the base arm, bringing a seed to ~$124 and three seeds to ~$372). One-step: 300 calls/seed at ~300 in / ~120 out = $2/seed. Cheap reduced scopes: one-step text only = $6 at 3 seeds; one-step plus multi-step-without-history = $190 at 3 seeds; single seed of everything = $236 (or $126 with the bug reproduced).

judgment.rule: ANALYSIS_PLAN section 1. Primary number: GPT-4 Turbo's text-only average accuracy over the 300 levels and three settings (published 1.87%). Survival = the re-run average (median of 3 seeds) stays inside the bootstrap 95% CI over levels of the original (n=300 per setting; at ~2% the CI is roughly +/-1.7 pp) AND the capability_limit direction holds, i.e. accuracy stays in the low single digits and hanoi/sudoku stay at or near 0. Partial = the level moves outside the CI but accuracy remains below 10%. Death = the model now solves a substantial share of levels (say >20% overall), which would retire the paper's 'MLLMs cannot play easy vision-based games yet' claim for this arm.
judgment.notes: Because the two multi-step text conditions are the same prompt in the released code, treat them as one condition with two draws rather than as a history ablation, and say so. Per-game structure is the more informative signal than the average: the published row's entire multi-step score comes from maze (14%), so a survival check should confirm that maze is still the only game with non-zero multi-step accuracy. If the frozen-board and empty-history bugs are repaired instead of reproduced, the run measures a different protocol and must be logged as a variant, not as a replication.

user_checks: Scope and budget: full text-only protocol at 3 seeds is ~$708 (~$372 if the empty-history bug is reproduced faithfully, since the history arm then costs the same as the base arm). Cheaper options: one-step only (~$6), one-step + multi-step-without-history (~$190), or a single seed of everything (~$236). Which?

Bug policy: reproduce the frozen-board and empty-history bugs verbatim - which is what the published numbers embody - or also run a repaired variant so the 'with history' condition actually has history? A repaired variant is a second, separately-labelled run, not a replication.
Snapshot: accept gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 by the date rule, given that the code asks a redacted gateway for 'gpt-4-turbo-128k' and the paper cites only the generic model page?

Code repairs needed before any paid run: fix the duplicated GPT4TurboInference class (the surviving one calls claude3_opus), add 'gpt4turbo' to the argparse choices, and replace the unbounded recursive retry with a bounded one. Confirm these three edits are acceptable as harness-level fixes rather than protocol changes.
domain_notes: This is the rare vision benchmark that fits a text-only runner: the paper evaluated GPT-4 Turbo in the text-only settings only (its three image-text cells in Table 1 are 'null'), so the levels arrive as ASCII matrices and JSON position lists rather than as PNGs and no multimodal path is needed. Everything else is in the repository - engines, solvers, prompts, 300 levels - which makes this a repository-based re-execution rather than a prompt-level one; the paper is not in the Tier B set. The interesting reproducibility finding is that the two multi-step text conditions are, in the released code, the same experiment run twice, and the published table shows exactly the signature of that: identical accuracies for the with- and without-history rows of both GPT-4 Turbo and Claude-3 Opus.
